blockingFindings.title: 1. Schema-repair re-prompt fallback is silently dropped from scope
blockingFindings.rationale: Issue #352 explicitly proposes three improvements, but the decision map resolves only the prompt clarification and the empty-array normalization. Its decision point "Do not hide malformed finding item objects, non-array field values, or invalid JSON behind normalization" means those cases keep throwing at the existing validation point (`parseSpecReviewJsonOutput`, review.js:2349-2352) — i.e. it implicitly drops the re-prompt fallback the issue asked for. These are materially different specs: a re-prompt fallback requires agent re-invocation, a dedicated repair prompt, and retry/termination handling, whereas normalization is a few lines of array defaulting. This is a scope inclusion/exclusion decision the user proposed and that conservative implementation cannot resolve without overriding the author's stated intent, so the spec cannot be bounded until the user confirms which scope applies.
blockingFindings.evidence: The user must decide whether the fix includes the issue's third proposed improvement — re-prompting the provider with a schema-repair-only prompt when output cannot be auto-filled — or whether scope is limited to passive normalization (auto-fill the two missing top-level arrays; let all other malformed output fail validation).
